questiontext.text:
Which of the following CANNOT be determined using a population Life table?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="member(1, ta_index)" ]]

The correct answer is The probability of literacy from any given age to any other given age.

The probability of literacy from any given age to any other given age has nothing to do with deaths or longevity of a human being

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(2, ta_index)" ]]

The correct answer is The probability of illness for any given number of persons at any age .

The probability of illness for any given number of persons at any age has nothing to do with deaths or longevity of a human being as it deals with epidemiology, specifically with the study of disease occurrence and distribution within populations.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(3, ta_index)" ]]

The correct answer is The probability of transmitting a disease from any given age to any other given age .

The probability of transmitting a disease from any given age to any other given age has nothing to do with deaths or longevity of a human being as it deals with epidemiology, specifically with the study of disease occurrence and distribution within populations.

[[/ if ]]
